turns.assistant_text:
### Kết luận
Liverpool đang tiến hành đàm phán với Paris Saint-Germain (PSG) về việc chuyển nhượng cầu thủ chạy cánh Bradley Barcola. Mặc dù đã có thỏa thuận sơ bộ giữa Barcola và Liverpool, hai câu lạc bộ vẫn còn cách xa trong việc định giá cầu thủ này, với PSG yêu cầu mức phí lên tới 170 triệu euro, mà Liverpool cho là quá cao.

### Những gì đã kiểm tra
- Liverpool đã có các cuộc thảo luận ban đầu về việc chuyển nhượng Bradley Barcola từ PSG.
- Barcola đã bày tỏ mong muốn gia nhập Liverpool và không có ý định gia hạn hợp đồng với PSG, nhưng mức phí chuyển nhượng vẫn là một trở ngại lớn.
- Các nguồn tin từ FOX Sports và Telecom Asia đều xác nhận thông tin này.

Cao, vì thông tin được xác nhận từ nhiều nguồn uy tín, bao gồm cả FOX Sports và Telecom Asia.

items.title: Liverpool Initiates Talks for PSG Winger Bradley Barcola - Telecom Asia Sport
items.summary: **Liverpool has held preliminary discussions regarding a potential transfer for PSG and France winger Bradley Barcola, although official contacts between the clubs have yet to commence. According to the source, the deal hinges on the transfer fee, as PSG values Bradley Barcola at €170 million. However, Liverpool considers this amount excessive and unrealistic, aiming to negotiate a transfer on more favorable terms, as the French winger is the Merseysiders' top transfer target this summer. The high asking price from PSG is attributed to the current market situation in the Premier League and significant deals within the English top flight, including Elliot Anderson's move to Manchester City and Morgan Rogers' transfer to Chelsea. Moreover, Liverpool believes that if an agreement is not reached this summer, PSG risks losing Bradley Barcola in 2027 for a significantly lower fee, as the player is not inclined to extend his contract.

items.title: France's Bradley Barcola Reaches Agreement To Join Liverpool From PSG - FOX Sports
items.summary: # France's Bradley Barcola Reaches Agreement To Join Liverpool From PSG. Paris Saint-Germain winger Bradley Barcola has reportedly reached an agreement in principle to join Liverpool following discussions with new manager Andoni Iraola. While the 23-year-old is eager to move to Anfield, the two clubs remain far apart in their valuation of the player. According to L'Équipe, Barcola has reached an agreement in principle to join Liverpool. The 23-year-old has informed the French champions that he does not intend to extend his current contract, which is set to expire in the summer of 2028. The same report claims that the France international recently held positive discussions with new Reds manager Iraola and several club executives to outline a potential move to Anfield. ## PSG Demand Massive Transfer Fee. While Barcola has agreed to the move in principle, completing the transfer remains a highly complex operation. However, Barcola's clear preference for a move to Anfield provides the Premier League side with a distinct advantage during these high-stakes discussions.

items.title: Why America's super rich have embraced the appeal of British soccer teams - CNBC
items.summary: * American ownership of Premier League clubs has steadily increased over the past several years. * Fenway Sports Group is poised to net a chunky return on investment from selling a minority stake in Liverpool FC. * CNBC explores how soccer has become such an attractive asset class in the eyes of investors stateside. English soccer clubs, or football clubs, per the sport's more common global name, have become hot commodities for ultra-rich and institutional ownership over the years. From Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney's fairy tale acquisition of a fifth-tier Welsh team captured by the "Welcome to Wrexham" TV series in 2020, to Snoop Dogg's investment in second-division side Swansea City this year, the appetite for collaborations with U.S. pop culture figures is only growing. Almost 16 years later, the Boston-based group is poised to net an enormous return on investment after FSG confirmed it is in talks with a syndicate of investors, led by British-Indian entrepreneur Amit Bhatia, to offload a significant minority stake in the club.

While Real Madrid and RB Leipzig remain confident of concluding a deal that will take Yan Diomande to the Spanish capital, they are still to reach an agreement, both on the fee and the structure of the payments, though that is expected to happen imminently. He is yet to receive permission to travel to Spain or to have a medical, but has already agreed personal terms with Madrid and has spoken with Jose Mourinho, the club’s new head coach, as part of that process.
